info.name: SathSawari · Shift Management
info.description:
Every endpoint added by the group / fleet shift management feature, in the order you would actually exercise them.

SETUP
1. Use the same environment as your existing Rideshare collection, it needs base-url and open_token.
2. Run the folders top to bottom. Almost every id is captured into an environment variable by a test script, so the flow chains on its own.
3. The OTPs come back in the response as tempOTP while you are not on production, so the verify steps chain automatically too.

TOKENS USED
  open_token          public endpoints
  admin_session       admin, roles and permissions
  owner_session       the driver who owns the fleet, ie the manager
  driver2_session     a second driver, later a sub manager
  passenger_session   a female passenger
  passenger2_session  a male passenger

Folder 4 contains two requests that are MEANT to fail, they are the proof of the clash and gender rules. Each one says so in its description.

request.description: Saves admin_session. Run this first if you want to touch roles or permissions.
group_owner and group_submanager are seeded at boot with their permissions already mapped. This also saves their ids.
The eight seeded permission codes. Saves a code -> id map you can use when remapping a role.
Proves point 14: a brand new role can be added with no code change.
Replaces the whole permission set of a role in one call. Read permission_ids_json from Get Permissions and paste the ids you want. Sending an empty list strips the role back to nothing.
A system role can have its description changed but never its name, because the group checks look those roles up by name.
Refused for a system role, and refused while any member still holds the role.
Step 1 of the flow. The owner of the fleet is an ordinary driver.
Saves owner_session and owner_driver_id.
The pin is needed to register a vehicle.

item.name: Owner Driver · Register Vehicle (7 seats, AC)

request.description: numberOfSeats, hasAC and hasHeating are what let this vehicle join a fleet. Seats are counted excluding the driver, so this van seats 7 passengers.
This driver will ask to join the fleet and later be made a sub manager.
hasAC and hasHeating are pointers on update, so leaving one out is different from switching it off.
Now returns numberOfSeats, hasAC and hasHeating.
Passengers had no account at all before this feature. Gender matters because seats are gender locked.
ACTIVATE_PASSENGER is its own operation, separate from ACTIVATE_DRIVER, so one number can hold both kinds of account.
Issues a passenger_token, a different token type from a driver's.
A second passenger of the other gender, used later to show the gender swap on a seat.
Verify with operation PASSENGER_FORGOT_PASSWORD and send the new password in the same body.
Parks the new password against the otp. Confirm it with operation PASSENGER_UPDATE_PASSWORD on /otp/verify.

request.description:
The whole week in one call, one row per day per direction.

Tuesday shows requirement 17.2: pickup is on, drop is off, so this passenger rides in the morning and makes their own way home.

Wednesday shows requirement 17.3: picked up from Gulberg Greens but dropped at Blue Area, a different place from the morning.

This form never creates a shift. It is only the sheet the manager reads while building one.
The creating driver becomes the owner, which in this product is the same thing as the manager. A group must be born with at least one vehicle, and every vehicle must already have declared its seats.

This is how a group id is discovered at all. Without it a driver could never learn the id that the join request needs.

Each row carries myStatus, so the app can tell 'ask to join' apart from 'waiting' without a second call. Empty means they have never asked.

Pass search to filter by name. Passengers hit the same thing at GET /api/v1/passenger/groups/search.

joinType is one of both, driver_only or vehicle_only (requirement 3).

driver_only must carry no vehicles. vehicle_only and both must carry at least one.

Nothing is granted here, the owner still decides. A driver who was turned down before can simply ask again.
Requirement 23. Note this runs on a passenger token, not a driver one.
Needs group.manage_members. Saves the membership row ids the next call decides on.

One call settles the whole queue. memberId is the id of the membership row, not of the driver or passenger behind it.

action is approve, reject or remove. approve and reject only act on somebody still waiting, remove only on somebody already inside.

The response splits into applied and skipped, and every skipped line says why, so a half valid batch still tells you exactly what happened. Deciding on a vehicle additionally needs group.manage_vehicles.

Requirement 16. The rule you insisted on is enforced here: a driver can only be promoted if they are ALREADY an approved member of this same fleet. Anybody else comes back in skipped with the reason, never promoted.

The owner can never be demoted, that would leave the fleet with nobody in charge.

A sub manager gets the four shift permissions and none of the membership ones.
The fleet with its driver, vehicle and passenger rosters. Only somebody already inside the fleet may look.

This is the sheet requirement 10 describes: who wants to travel on this day in this direction, from where, at what time, and which gender seat they need.

Leave day_of_week and direction off to get the whole week.

Gated on shift.assign_seats rather than plain membership, since it carries home addresses, so the owner and sub managers see it and an ordinary joined driver does not.
The same discovery list seen through a passenger token.
The fleets a passenger has been let into or is still waiting on, so they can see where their request stands.

The brief says people can join AND leave, and until now only the manager could take somebody out.

Refused while shifts are still expecting this driver behind the wheel, since a driver cannot be swapped out automatically. Cancel or reassign those first.

Their vehicles leave the fleet with them, and any sub manager role is dropped. The owner can never leave, they delete the group instead.

Run this AFTER you have finished with the sub manager shift, or it will refuse.

A departing passenger's seats on upcoming shifts are freed automatically and each affected shift's taken count is put back in step, so they never leave a ghost sitting in a seat nobody can fill.

The same release happens when a manager removes a passenger through the bulk decide endpoint.
Refused while the fleet still has shifts ahead of it. Cancel those first. Run this last, it ends the flow.

request.description:
The stops are the route, in the order you send them, and each seat hangs off the stop its passenger waits at (your ordered stop requirement). The last stop here is the destination and carries nobody.

Every seat of the vehicle gets a row, so this 7 seat van comes back with 2 assigned and 5 empty seats a manager can fill later.

makeTemplate saves the shape for reuse, exactly like ride templates. There is no separate build from template api, the app refetches a template and posts it back here.

Rejected if the vehicle or the driver is already promised at that hour, on another shift OR on a carpool ride (requirements 19 to 22).

request.description:
The same people going home is a COMPLETELY SEPARATE shift with its own route (requirements 12, 13 and 17.4). Note the stop order is reversed and the drop points differ from the morning pickup points.

It does not clash with the morning shift because the time windows do not overlap.

Returns the shift, its stops in order, and every seat.

The shift carries both the driver's number and the number of the manager who built it, which is the contact information you asked to be on every shift.

Visible to any approved member of the fleet, and to a passenger holding a seat on it.
The manager's roster view. Every filter is optional.
What this driver is driving.
The same handler seen through a passenger token: the shifts they hold a seat on, morning and evening both.
A passenger can open a shift they are seated on, and gets the driver and manager contacts with it.

item.name: Swap Male Rider For Female (one call)

request.description:
The swap you asked for. Seat 2 held a male rider and now holds a female one, and seat 1 goes the other way, in a single request.

The rule that still holds: a seat's declared gender and the person sitting in it must always agree, so nobody ever lands in a seat kept for the other gender. Try changing one gender field and leaving the passenger, it will be refused.

stopSequence points at the stop that passenger now waits at, counting from 1.

Send passengerId as "" to free a seat. Everybody whose place actually changed is notified, people who kept their seat are left alone.
An empty passengerId frees the seat and clears the gender it was kept for. seatsTaken is recomputed.

Requirement 16 end to end: the sub manager takes the shift building load off the owner. Same endpoint, different token.

Try the group membership calls on this token and they will come back 'Operation is not permitted', because a sub manager holds the shift permissions and none of the membership ones.

request.description:
EXPECTED TO FAIL with 'Vehicle already has a ride or a shift scheduled for this duration'. This proves requirements 19 and 20.

Create a carpool ride on this same vehicle at this time and the shift is refused too, and the mirror holds: creating a carpool ride while a shift is on gets refused as well (requirements 21 and 22).

Pushes the whole trip back twenty minutes WITHOUT losing the seat plan. Cancelling and rebuilding would throw the seats away, and is refused outright inside the two hour window.

Every field except shiftId is optional, but the time window has to be sent whole or not at all. stopTimes matches stops by their sequence number, so stop ids and the seats hanging off them survive.

Moving the window re-runs the full clash check, ignoring this shift's own row. Everybody aboard is notified.

The vehicle and driver are deliberately NOT changeable here, swapping either can invalidate every seat, so that stays a cancel and rebuild.

Soft cancel. Refused when the shift starts within 2 hours, mirroring the carpool ride guard, so use a shift comfortably in the future.

The driver and every seated passenger are told, with the manager's contact in the message.

A template comes back with its stops, its seat plan and its vehicle.

This is how a shift is rebuilt: the app fetches a template, prefills the create form with it, changes the date, and posts it to POST /api/v1/shift. Exactly the pattern your ride templates already use, which is why there is no build from template endpoint.

Template seats point at their stop by sequence rather than by id, so a template stays valid for a brand new shift.
Deletes the template with its stops and seats. Needs shift.manage_templates.
